explanation: In the US, patting a child on the head is a common, affectionate gesture, but doing the same to an adult you're not close to can come across as condescending or overly familiar - Americans generally keep greetings to handshake-level contact and reserve head-touching for close relationships. It isn't taboo or deeply offensive, just socially awkward outside family or close-friend contexts.
local_tip: Stick to a handshake, high-five, or a pat on the shoulder with adults; save head-pats for children or people you know very well.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred part of the body; touching anyone's head, including children's, is a serious offense.
Patting a child's head can be affectionate, but doing so to an adult, especially an elder, is seen as disrespectful.
Public physical contact is minimal; patting someone's head is seen as overly familiar rather than a serious offense.

sources.title: 12 American Habits That Come Off as Rude Overseas
